similar_scenes.name: Blues rock británico
similar_scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
similar_scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
similar_scenes.desc: La «gramática» del heavy: su estructura de canción, sus progresiones y sus riffs vienen del blues eléctrico urbano de Muddy Waters y Howlin’ Wolf, pero de segunda mano, ya «rockeado» por los grupos británicos de guitarra. El gran mediador son los Yardbirds y su sucesión de solistas (Eric Clapton, Jeff Beck y Jimmy Page), que veneraban a los bluesmen negros sin imitarlos servilmente. Cream (y Clapton, según él mismo) inventa el solo largo para estirar media hora de repertorio, y el público lo convierte en convención. El virtuosismo de la guitarra solista es la mayor herencia del blues rock al heavy.
similar_scenes.family: Raíces: blues rock, psicodelia y hard rock

similar_scenes.name: Blues revival y blues-rock
similar_scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
similar_scenes.desc: John Mayall define con Bluesbreakers (con Eric Clapton) el rhythm'n'blues tocado por blancos europeos, el blues-rock, y siembra el progresivo con sus discos de jazz y lounge. Su equivalente americano es Al Kooper (Blues Project, Supersession, Blood Sweat & Tears). Cream, el primer power-trio, cambia la cara del rock británico con improvisación de jazz, distorsión y solos interminables; Fleetwood Mac de Peter Green y Ten Years After llevan del blues al hard rock. En San Francisco, Janis Joplin, Steve Miller y Santana; en Los Ángeles, Taj Mahal y Ry Cooder reconstruyen las tradiciones; Bob Seger casa el grito soul con el Detroit obrero.

podcast.title: Post-1978 Rock Diversification
podcast.body: Blues rock was a genre that became a specific point of discussion within mainstream rock after 1978, reflecting the new complexity in music categorization. "People were now talking about metal and Prague and folk rock, and soft rock, and country rock, and blues rock, and of course, punk."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Post-Punk Explosion Part 1: New Wave

podcast.title: Blues Rock → Hard Rock → Heavy Metal; Heavy Metal Term Popularized by Steppenwolf
podcast.body: Blues Rock became the progenitor of Hard Rock, a term that began appearing around 1968, which led into Heavy Metal by the end of the decade. Heavy metal was largely a British invention — Led Zeppelin, Black Sabbath, Deep Purple — though the term "Heavy Metal" itself was popularized by the Canadian singer John Kay of Steppenwolf. "Blues Rock became known as the progenitor of Hard Rock, a term that began showing up around 1968, which led us into heavy metal by the end of the decade."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Fleetwood Mac Style
podcast.body: Fleetwood Mac originated as British blues rock hitmakers in their early days. Christine McVie's songwriting, as seen in "You Make Loving Fun," later echoed her earlier "woolly blues rock" style from the early 1970s. "We talked about the formation of transatlantic band Fleetwood Mac and how the songwriting of the late Christine McVee carried them from their early days as British blues rock hitmakers through along early 70s dry spell."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Early Sound of The Tragically Hip
podcast.body: The Tragically Hip's early performances, particularly in Eastern Ontario venues like the Tarapin Tavern and Lakeview Manor, largely featured blues rock standards. Their setlists included material from influential artists such as The Rolling Stones, The Doors, The Yardbirds, Marvin Gaye, Otis Redding, and Van Morrison. "Their set consisted largely of blues rock standards. Early stuff from the stones, material from the doors, the yard birds, Marvin Gaye, Otis Redding, Ben Morrison, that kind of thing."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
